CrowdStrike::workday::R30742.raw_text: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you. About The Role: CrowdStrike's Falcon sensor runs on millions of endpoints globally, protecting more than half of the Fortune 500 companies. It's a high-performance, lightweight agent that detects and prevents sophisticated threats in real-time. It's one of the most widely deployed security platforms in the world, running across every major OS and architecture. Every Falcon sensor release ships to millions of endpoints, so knowing a release is healthy — and being able to prove it — is a high-stakes problem. We're looking for a Software Engineer to design and build the systems, metrics, and dashboards that give engineers and leadership one clear, trusted picture of sensor and release health. You'll join a small team of 4 engineers (remote and hybrid) focused on the metrics, dashboards, and developer tooling that give visibility into the overall health of our build system — tools that sensor engineers and leadership rely on every day. You'll start in our repo-health rotation to see firsthand where sensor teams get stuck — and continue building the automation that replaces that manual process with AI-assisted signals, so attention goes to the highest-priority work. This role sits at the intersection of developer tooling, metrics, and release quality. You'll work primarily in Python and Django on the backend, and React and CSS on the front end, turning raw signal into clear, actionable insight. We're also building out agentic workflows with Claude Code — you'll help create the skills and commands that both our automated systems and the sensor engineering team use day to day, solving problems like: How do we know a sensor repo is unhealthy before it becomes a crisis? How do we give every stakeholder a single source of truth on release quality? How do we quantify the health of the tools and processes our team owns? This role is a hybrid role with an expectation of at least 2x days in office each week, working out of one of the posted locations. What You'll Do: Design and build our sensor quality dashboard from the ground up, giving engineers and leadership full visibility into the health of active sensor releases across multiple metrics Own the process of defining new signals and metrics for repo and release health, and instrument the systems needed to capture them Spend time in our repo-health rotation, partnering with sensor teams to see firsthand where engineers get stuck — then build the tooling that fixes it Build and maintain metrics and visibility across all tooling and processes owned by our team Build and extend Claude Code skills, commands, and agentic workflows used by both our automated systems and the sensor engineering team Drive improvements by identifying gaps in visibility, prototyping solutions, and shipping dashboards and tooling that measurably improve how our team and stakeholders understand sensor health Work with our data stack — LogScale, PostgreSQL, and Valkey — to collect, process, and surface sensor health metrics reliably What You'll Need: 3+ years building production systems with a focus on developer tooling, metrics, or observability/monitoring Strong Python experience (we build on Django) Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes. Micron::workday::JR116566.raw_text: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Key Responsibilities: Work closely with multiple teams across IT, Information Security, Technology, and business functions to drive impactful change. Design, develop, integrate, and support scalable enterprise solutions across Kinaxis, SAP, Blue Yonder (BY), and related enterprise planning applications . Analyze and troubleshoot complex system and integration issues across Kinaxis, SAP, and BY , leveraging Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, and AI-Enabled tools where applicable to accelerate problem solving and improve productivity. Understand end-to-end business processes, system integrations, and data flows across enterprise planning platforms, and assess upstream and downstream impacts of application and software changes. Leverage data and AI Assisted analysis to support impact assessment, root-cause analysis, solution design, testing, and continuous improvement. Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams on end-to-end integration testing, system validation, and performance analysis; resolve issues, proactively identify opportunities for improvement, and drive initiatives through completion. Leverage AI Assistants and Large Language Models (LLMs) , where appropriate, to support software development, analysis, automation, testing, troubleshooting, and technical documentation while maintaining appropriate human review and accountability. Identify opportunities for AI-Enabled and Agentic AI solutions , automation, and process improvements across enterprise planning and supply chain applications. As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future. We offer a choice of medical, dental and vision plans in all locations enabling team members to select the plans that best meet their family healthcare needs and budget. Micron::workday::JR116017.raw_text: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Our Opportunity Summary: At Micron, we build memory and storage solutions that power the technologies changing how the world works, learns, and connects. We're looking for passionate people to join us and help grow and innovate in the semiconductor industry. As a Process Control Systems Engineer, you'll develop, deploy, and sustain Run-to-Run (R2R) and Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) strategies. These strategies protect process stability, yield, and quality across wafer fabrication. You'll work with manufacturing, engineering, and information systems teams on site, and with counterparts worldwide. (Disclaimer ) While you may not exhibit all of the characteristics/skills listed below today, we are highly interested in a team member who is anxious to grow in both technical breadth and depth. If you are open to learning from and being a valued member of a team of top-tier engineers, we are eager to help build on your existing foundation and expand your individual and collaborative skills in this exciting and unique opportunity. What’s Encouraged Daily: Partner with manufacturing and engineering customers to define control requirements and choose the right R2R and FDC solutions. Develop, deploy, and maintain R2R controllers and FDC strategies, including data collection, limits, and out-of-control action plans (OCAPs). Monitor controller and strategy performance, and use data analysis to improve existing control methods. Use AMAT E3 to implement strategy enhancements and bug fixes, and develop smaller R2R code modules or sub-strategies. Configure data collection and troubleshoot strategy, tool, system, and communication issues across Host, CIM, and Sigma. Investigate process variation and excursions, find root causes, and drive corrective actions. Follow worldwide business rules and best known methods (BKMs), manage changes through change management, and document all strategies and changes. Deliver R2R training, share lessons learned with global teams, and lead small teams on quality and cost-improvement projects. How To Qualify: Shown through education, internships, research, military, manufacturing, or professional experience. Bachelor's degree or advanced certification in a related technical field, OR equivalent technical military experience, OR an equivalent mix of education and relevant experience. Knowledge of process control methods, including SPC, R2R, and FDC. Experience with data analysis, root cause analysis, and corrective action in a manufacturing environment. Ability to troubleshoot software, system, and equipment communication issues. Strong communication and documentation skills, and experience working across functions. What Sets You Apart: Hands-on experience with AMAT E3 (R2R, FDC, SPC/SPACE modules). Familiarity with CIM, MES, APC, and GEM/SECS systems in high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. Experience with change management, BKMs, and controlled documentation in a global, multi-site environment. Experience leading small technical teams or projects, and delivering training to end users. Experience and/or interest in developing Agentic AI workflows into current or future processes. Our team vision is a continuing desire to develop your skills working in an inclusive, diverse environment of multicultural Teams across worldwide geographies! Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. As a Product Engineer in the High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Media Health (MH) team, you will work with Fab, Yield Improvement, Design, and other engineering groups passionately focused on HBM. You will develop, deploy, optimize, and innovate test strategies for Micron's DRAM in HBM products. The team acts as a key partner of these engineering groups and specialties, focusing on innovating new and improved test strategies and features. You will guide development for Probe (wafer level test), Burn-in, and ATE test code and testing techniques used to validate and ensure device performance. You will assist in debugging code and aiding other specialists in the characterization of applicable HBM devices. In this role, your additional responsibilities include an in-depth understanding of general device functionality specific to HBM products as well as schematics and signal integrity. Responsibilities: Work with Design Engineering to run simulations pre-silicon to validate DFT circuits and test modes as well as communicate design issues found. Work on pre-silicon tasks with MH and test teams to define required tester resources. Work with Test Engineering and HBM Product Engineering to ensure specific product requirements or limitations are comprehended, leading to silicon performance matching expectations. This work includes test program debug, examination of data, and test development. Support the ID1 fabrication site Process Integration and Yield Enhancement through test development, DOE data analysis, focusing on the impact of test on product yield and quality. Debug and identify root causes for failures using data, electrical and physical analysis techniques. Use AI with existing engineering tools to improve test flows, test strategies, and enhance yield. Supervise yields to ensure they are meeting projections and expeditiously investigate root causes when they are not. Provide technical training and expertise. This includes providing On-The-Job training for new engineers, assisting with data interpretation, acting as a product-specific point of contact and attending technical seminars. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering (Master's Degree preferred) with 3 years experience in DRAM or other memory testing experience. Craft and deliver presentations for meetings with partner teams. Support critical Micron initiatives through support of high-value-added projects. Automate routine engineering tasks using AI augmented scripts, data analysis, and reporting. Preferred Qualification: Understanding of semiconductor fabrication process, defectivity and marginality, and degradation mechanisms. Basic analog and digital circuit design and understanding. Programming experience in C, C++, and Python. Familiarity with using engineering tools in a Linux environment as well as Linux command line skills. Familiarity with AI tools such as Claude Code for engineering development tasks. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you. About The Role: CrowdStrike Falcon is a two-component security product. One component is the "Sensor" — a lightweight agent installed on endpoint systems that observes system activity, recognizes malicious behavior, provides on-box prevention capability, and sends telemetry to the Falcon cloud. The cloud component aggregates Sensor telemetry across each customer's network, correlates malicious behavior across machines, and presents security teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments. The Falcon Sensor runs on tens of millions of endpoints worldwide, across Windows, macOS and Linux, in both user mode and kernel mode. Engineering software at that depth and that scale is among the hardest problems in the industry, and CrowdStrike holds the Sensor to an exceptionally high standard of quality, performance and engineering rigor. Sustaining that standard requires a team with true mastery of what software does at runtime, at the lowest levels of the stack. That team is Sensor Performance and Reliability — CrowdStrike's team of debug engineers. Deep runtime analysis is our craft: postmortem memory dump analysis, disassembly and reverse engineering, and source-level analysis, used to explain with precision and evidence how low-level code behaves on real systems. It is one of the most technically demanding specialties in systems engineering, and very few organizations invest in it as a discipline in its own right. We do, because at our scale the answer to "what exactly happened, and why?" has to be exact rather than approximate. Our mandate goes further than answering that question well. We're chartered to turn what we learn from deep analysis into durable engineering improvements — strengthening diagnostics, tooling, validation coverage and development practices so that lessons generalize far beyond the investigation that produced them, and so that the next analysis is faster than the last. Our work makes the product stronger, and it raises the engineering capability of every team we work with. We are hiring an entry-level engineer to join us in that mission. We do not expect you to arrive with deep Windows internals, assembly, or reverse engineering experience. Those are skills we will teach you, and you will learn them from engineers who operate at the top of this field. What we are looking for is a strong programmer with excellent problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity about how computers actually work underneath the abstractions — someone who is drawn to a hard, ambiguous problem rather than put off by it. If you are the kind of person who cannot leave a mystery alone until you understand it completely, this is an unusually good place to build a career. Location: This is a hybrid role based out of one of the posted locations: Redmond, WA or Sunnyvale, CA , with a combination of in-office and remote work. What You'll Do: Analyze the runtime behavior of complex low-level software across user mode and kernel mode on Windows, primarily through postmortem memory dump analysis in WinDbg. Work from raw memory, register state and disassembly to a precise, evidence-backed account of what executing code did and why — and hold yourself to a high evidentiary bar in reaching it. Correlate your analysis with source code, applying reverse engineering and disassembly techniques where symbols, source or context are incomplete. Drive investigations to accurate, well-reasoned conclusions rather than plausible-sounding ones, and communicate confidence and uncertainty honestly. Partner with Sensor development teams to translate your findings into concrete, well-designed engineering improvements. Generalize from individual investigations: recognize patterns, and champion improvements to tooling, diagnostics, automated validation and engineering practice that raise the reliability bar broadly rather than locally. Build and improve the tooling, automation and analysis techniques that make deep runtime analysis faster, more repeatable and more accessible — for our team and for Sensor engineers across the company. Write clearly and precisely for engineering, quality and leadership audiences. A first-rate technical analysis is only as valuable as its reader's ability to act on it. Collaborate with engineering teams across multiple locations and timezones, including Sensor platform, detection and OS-specialist teams. What You'll Need: BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Solid working knowledge of C and C++, and the ability to read and reason about code you did not write. Good foundational knowledge of data structures and algorithms. Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, and comfort working with incomplete information — much of this work involves reconstructing runtime behavior from partial evidence. Genuine curiosity about systems fundamentals: operating system internals, computer architecture, memory management, concurrency, compilers and assembly. You should want to learn these deeply. Persistence and intellectual honesty: the willingness to keep digging until you actually know the answer, and to say clearly when you don't yet. Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to take ownership of your work and follow it through to resolution. Ability to communicate, collaborate, and work effectively in a globally distributed team. Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes. Bonus Points: Any exposure to debugging tools and techniques — WinDbg, GDB, LLDB, or similar — including as a hobby, in coursework, or in CTFs. Coursework, internships, or personal projects involving operating system internals, kernel or driver development, systems programming, or computer architecture. Familiarity with x86-64 or ARM64 assembly and the ability to read disassembly. Exposure to reverse engineering, malware analysis, or vulnerability research. Experience with Windows internals specifically (processes, threads, virtual memory, synchronization, the Windows kernel and driver model). Scripting experience, particularly Python, for automation and analysis tooling. Key Responsibilities Find the test gaps that matter. Use field failures, factory nonconformances, failure analysis, 8D findings, FMEA/FMECA risks, and test data to identify where existing assurance methods failed to detect risk before shipment. Translate failure mechanisms into testable requirements. Convert complex failure signatures and real-world operating conditions into specific, measurable, and defensible requirements that engineering teams and suppliers can execute. Engineer system-representative test coverage. Define the functional, parametric, stress, burn-in, thermal, RF, high-voltage, leak, particle, interlock, and other tests needed to expose targeted failure modes before they reach an Applied factory or customer. Resolve implementation issues, coordinate engineering changes, and ensure the solution is practical, scalable, and ready for production use. Preserve test effectiveness throughout the lifecycle. Establish the preventive-maintenance, calibration, out-of-tolerance response, configuration control, data retention, and performance-monitoring requirements necessary to keep deployed test systems reliable and effective. Measure outcomes, not activity. Monitor detection effectiveness, test-system performance, false failures, escapes, NCs, DMRs, and other relevant quality and operational indicators. Use the results to verify effectiveness and identify the next improvement opportunity. Prevent recurrence at the source. Apply lessons from escapes to improve supplier test mandates, Functional Requirements Documents, FMEA/FMECA, Design for Testability, and applicable product-lifecycle deliverables so that prevention becomes part of how future products are developed. Lead across organizational boundaries. Drive multiple complex initiatives across suppliers, factories, Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Supplier Engineering, NPI Quality, Product Quality & Reliability, and business-unit teams. Communicate technical conclusions, risks, decisions, and business impact with clarity. Build scalable Test Excellence capability. Create reusable requirements, methods, standards, specifications, and validation practices. Mentor other engineers, transfer knowledge, and raise the organization’s ability to find the right problems and solve them permanently. You will turn real-world failures and emerging risks into test solutions that prevent defects from reaching our factories and customers. From defining system-representative requirements to developing, validating, and deploying test fixtures, you will own the solution from insight to sustained impact. You will challenge assumptions with evidence, work across suppliers and engineering teams, and help build the methods and standards that define Test Excellence globally. Micron::workday::JR116695.title: Information Security Engineer – Global Security Infrastructure
Micron::workday::JR116695.raw_text: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Micron is expanding and modernizing its global footprint, and physical security technology has to keep pace. Sites today run a mix of systems at different ages and maturity levels. Our goal is a consistent, standards-based security infrastructure everywhere we operate, covering video surveillance and analytics, access control, intrusion detection, visitor management, and perimeter protection. Modern security systems are connected, technology-based platforms, and we want them deployed on predictable schedules and managed as a product, not a collection of one-off projects. In partnership with the Global Security Operations leadership team, you will own that rollout end to end: planning, sequencing, site readiness, execution, and measurement. You will treat security operators and site leaders as your customers, gather their requirements, and make sure what we deploy works for them. Responsibilities: Own the global rollout program. Build and run the multi-year, multi-site deployment plan for physical security infrastructure upgrades. Sequence sites by risk and readiness, manage scope, schedule, budget, and dependencies, and keep simultaneous projects across regions moving. Turn standards into repeatable deployments. Partner with security engineering to translate technology standards and reference designs into deployment playbooks, site readiness checklists, and acceptance criteria so that every site rollout looks the same and gets faster over time. Bring a product mindset. Gather requirements from security operators, site security leaders, and regional teams. Run the program with agile practices: prioritize a backlog, define what "done" looks like for each site, iterate on the playbook, and measure whether deployed systems deliver the expected operational outcomes. Build AI-enabled tooling and automation. Develop or adopt tools for deployment tracking, configuration standards checks, device health monitoring, and asset and lifecycle management across the global fleet. Use AI tools and agents to speed up program work such as site assessments, status reporting, risk identification, and documentation. Ensure deployed systems, including AI video analytics, produce data that integrates cleanly with the team's security operations data platform. Coordinate partners and integrators. Manage external integrators and contractors through statements of work, schedules, and quality checks. Coordinate closely with IT and network teams, Information Security (for device hardening and network segmentation), Facilities and construction teams (especially for new fab builds), and EHS. Govern and verify. Establish a governance cadence for the program, track site compliance against security technology standards, and run post-deployment audits to confirm systems are installed, configured, and operating as designed. Manage risk and change. Identify and raise program risks early, drive decisions to resolution, and plan for operator training and cutover so new systems are adopted, not just installed. Report to leadership. Build clear metrics and dashboards on rollout progress, spend, site compliance, and system health. Present status, risks, and trade-offs to senior leadership in concise, executive-ready form. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience, plus 5+ years in software product management or software engineering, including ownership of delivering a product or platform to users. Experience leading cross-functional delivery with multiple teams and external partners, including managing scope, schedule, and budget. Working knowledge of networked systems, APIs, and integrations, plus scripting or data analysis skills sufficient to build tooling, automate reporting, and hold technical conversations with engineers and integrators. AI proficiency: hands-on use of generative AI tools (e.g., copilots, LLM-based assistants, or agents) in day-to-day work, with judgment about where AI output needs human review. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including building executive-level status reports and presentations, and willingness to travel domestically and internationally. Preferred Qualifications: Experience rolling out technology across many sites or regions with global teams (for example IoT or edge device fleets, enterprise infrastructure, or manufacturing systems). Experience with device fleet management, configuration management, or monitoring and observability tools, including applying AI/ML for anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, or automated workflows. Experience with construction, facilities, or capital projects, including managing integrators or contractors through SOWs and acceptance testing. Exposure to physical security systems such as video surveillance, access control, or intrusion detection, ideally in semiconductor, manufacturing, or other high-security industrial environments. Agile certification (e.g., CSM, PSM, SAFe, or PMI-ACP). As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future. We offer a choice of medical, dental and vision plans in all locations enabling team members to select the plans that best meet their family healthcare needs and budget. Micron also provides benefit programs that help protect your income if you are unable to work due to illness or injury, and paid family leave. Additionally, Micron benefits include a robust paid time-off program and paid holidays. For additional information regarding the Benefit programs available, please see the Benefits Guide posted on micron.com/careers/benefits . What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters Salesforce is seeking a Systems Engineer to support the technical operation, reliability, and continued evolution of Marketing Cloud Engagement (MCE). This individual will partner with Marketing, Product, and Data to support MCE operations. This is a hands-on technical operations and implementation role. You will co-own key MCE capabilities including Preference Center, Global Footer, Journey Builder, Automation Studio, Data Extension management, DE audience and segmentation logic, and Mobile Push. You will translate business needs into scalable technical solutions, troubleshoot complex production issues, and improve the operating model for customer-facing messaging. The role is ideal for an individual who is comfortable working at the intersection of marketing technology, data, automation, and production support. Core Responsibilities & Scope Build, configure, test, and maintain email and mobile messaging journeys in Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement. Use Journey Builder and Automation Studio to implement customer journeys, triggered communications, scheduled automations, data imports, and operational workflows. Write query plan optimized SQL queries with complicating joins Design, manage, and troubleshoot Data Extensions, data models, SQL queries, audience tables, suppression logic, and automation dependencies. Support Preference Center and subscription-management experiences, including consent, unsubscribe processing, compliance controls, localization, and subscriber-state troubleshooting. Own and evolve Global Footer implementations and reusable messaging components across campaigns, regions, and communication types. Support MCE Mobile Push campaigns, including audience targeting, segment qualification, exclusions, message configuration, send readiness, delivery monitoring, and event-week operational coverage. Diagnose issues involving missing or stale source data, empty or incorrect audiences, duplicate-send risk, automation failures, journey entry and exit logic, and delayed or failed sends. Validate audience counts, representative audience members, source-data freshness, exclusions, and send configuration before production launches. Partner with Marketing and Product stakeholders to turn business requirements into technical solution documents, configuration plans, implementation steps, test cases, and operational runbooks. Collaborate with upstream data owners, segmentation teams, mobile teams, and platform engineering teams to resolve dependencies and establish clear escalation paths. Participate in incident response for MCE capabilities, including triage, investigation, stakeholder communication, escalation, resolution, and follow-up. Participate in a formal on-call rotation (e.g., PagerDuty) to support critical incident response, triage, and resolution outside of standard business hours. Improve monitoring, alert quality, dashboards, documentation, operational controls, and incident-prevention practices for messaging systems. Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, reduce operational risk, improve compliance safeguards, and make campaign delivery more reliable at scale. Maintain appropriate standards for data privacy, consent management, localization, testing, change management, and customer-impacting production work. Minimum Requirements 5 years of working with Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement at large scale companies. Hands-on experience with Journey Builder, Automation Studio, Data Extensions, SQL Query Activities, and email-send or campaign-execution workflows. Strong SQL skills, including audience qualification, deduplication, suppression, segmentation, and data-validation queries. Experience troubleshooting production workflows involving data ingestion, automations, audience selection, journey logic, and message delivery. Experience translating business requirements into clear technical designs, implementation documentation, and validation plans. Ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical partners, including marketers, product managers, analysts, and data engineers. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and comfort operating in time-sensitive production environments. Excellent written communication skills, including the ability to produce clear technical documentation and status updates. Experience with AMPscript, HTML, CSS, email templates, content blocks, CloudPages, or triggered sends. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Preference Center, consent-management, unsubscribe, subscription, or privacy-compliance workflows. Experience supporting mobile push-notification campaigns, including targeting, audience readiness, delivery monitoring, and incident response. Experience operating reusable global email components or localized footer and compliance content. Familiarity with Salesforce Data Cloud and its MCE connector Experience with monitoring, dashboards, logs, alerting, or incident-management platforms such as PagerDuty. Experience supporting high-visibility campaigns, large events, or customer-facing communications with strict execution windows. Familiarity with localization and regional messaging requirements, including content, consent, and footer variations by country or language. Success in This Role A successful individual in this role will become a trusted technical owner for Marketing Cloud Engagement operations. They will support and improve journey execution, audience and data workflows, preference-management experiences, global email components, and mobile push programs. They will help the organization move from reactive campaign support toward a more reliable, documented, observable, and scalable messaging platform. Micron::workday::JR116959.title: Offensive Security AI Engineer
Micron::workday::JR116959.raw_text: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The Offensive Security AI Engineer will plan and implement adversary-informed security testing across Micron's technology environment. The role is intentionally broader than AI security: the engineer will assess web and mobile applications, APIs, cloud services, identity platforms, enterprise infrastructure, endpoints, wireless environments, security controls, and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled systems. AI will be used as a force multiplier throughout the testing lifecycle. The engineer will apply AI-assisted techniques to accelerate reconnaissance, analyze attack paths, develop and debug tooling, generate and refine test cases, support evidence analysis, and improve reporting quality. The engineer evaluates AI and machine learning systems when applicable. This covers their models, applications, data flows, integrations, guardrails, and infrastructure. This position will partner with security, engineering, technology, and business teams to communicate risk, validate mitigations, transfer offensive security knowledge, and improve defensive readiness. The successful candidate will balance deep technical execution with sound judgment, responsible use of AI, clear documentation, and effective communication with both technical and non-technical audiences. Responsibilities : Plan, implement, lead, and report on internal and external penetration tests, red team operations, purple team exercises, and targeted security assessments. Discover, validate, and safely exploit vulnerabilities end to end across web applications, APIs, cloud platforms, identity systems, networks, endpoints, mobile applications, wireless environments, products, and security controls. Use AI-assisted workflows to improve reconnaissance, attack-path analysis, test-case development, code review, exploit research, tooling, evidence analysis, and reporting while independently validating AI-generated output. Develop, customize, and maintain offensive security tooling, scripts, automation, and proof-of-concept code that increase the scale, consistency, and repeatability of testing. Assess AI and machine learning systems when in scope, including model behavior, application logic, retrieval and data pipelines, agents and tools, access controls, integrations, guardrails, and infrastructure dependencies. Emulate realistic adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures to evaluate prevention, detection, investigation, and response capabilities while operating within approved rules of engagement. Evaluate proposed architecture and design decisions to identify attack paths, trust-boundary weaknesses, insecure assumptions, and gaps in secure design principles. Collaborate with multi-functional partners to explain findings, prioritize remediation, implement corrective actions, and translate technical risk into business impact. Minimum Qualifications : Significant experience participating in and leading offensive security operations, including penetration testing or red team engagements. Practical experience testing multiple technology domains, such as applications, APIs, cloud, identity, infrastructure, endpoints, mobile, wireless, or security controls. Working knowledge of AI and large language model security concepts, common attack surfaces, and the risks introduced by models, data, agents, tools, and integrations. Proficiency in Python, C#, Go, PowerShell, or another language used for security tooling and automation. Strong written, presentation, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain highly technical issues to non-technical audiences. Preferred Qualifications: Industry-recognized offensive security certifications such as OSCP, OSEP, OSCE3, CRTO, GPEN, GXPN, PNPT, or comparable credentials. Experience building reusable automation, security testing frameworks, agentic workflows, or integrations that support offensive security operations.
